original_title: Multiple Switch 2 Editions Were Announced Today, But One Big Exception Remains
summary_en: Nintendo has revealed several 'Switch 2 Editions' for upcoming and existing titles, but a glaring omission has left fans questioning the fate of a beloved fighting game. The new versions promise enhanced experiences, yet one major franchise remains conspicuously absent.
ai_analysis: This news highlights Nintendo's strategy of iterative hardware upgrades, with developers opting for 'enhanced editions' rather than full-blown sequels for some of their biggest hits, leaving the door open for franchise dormancy or future surprise announcements.

en.title: Switch 2 Editions Announced: Smash Bros. Ultimate Still Left Out
en.summary: Nintendo has revealed several 'Switch 2 Editions' for upcoming and existing titles, but a glaring omission has left fans questioning the fate of a beloved fighting game. The new versions promise enhanced experiences, yet one major franchise remains conspicuously absent.
en.body:
The gaming landscape is abuzz following the latest Nintendo Direct, which showcased a wave of 'Switch 2 Editions' for a handful of prominent titles. While this signals Nintendo's continued commitment to leveraging its established franchises on new hardware, it also brings a significant question to the forefront: why is **Super Smash Bros. Ultimate** still seemingly left behind?

As of today, the fighting game juggernaut remains without any announced Switch 2-related update, a fact that has persisted since its initial release. This is particularly noteworthy given that **Super Smash Bros. Ultimate** is the third best-selling game on the original Nintendo Switch, a fact that makes its exclusion from the list of games receiving 'free updates for select Nintendo Switch games' on Nintendo's official website all the more puzzling. The silence surrounding a potential Switch 2 version, especially after nearly five years since its final update with **Sora**'s reveal, has led many to believe the franchise is currently dormant on the platform.

## Enhanced Editions Arrive for Select Titles

Despite the **Smash Bros.** omission, Nintendo has indeed confirmed Switch 2 upgrades for other major games. Six titles are set to receive the 'Switch 2 Edition' treatment, a mix of first-party and third-party offerings. **Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity Definitive Edition** is leading the charge, promising all Expansion Pass DLC, improved visuals and frame rates, more enemies on screen, and a new 'Calamity Mode.' Although branded as 'Definitive Edition,' Nintendo is explicitly calling it an 'enhanced Nintendo Switch 2 version.'

Perhaps more surprisingly, **Pikmin 4** is also getting an upgrade, set to include voice commands for the trusty canine **Oatchi** and a new 'Dandori Academy' mode on November 12. Rounding out the first-party announcements is **Xenoblade Chronicles 3**, which will also receive the Switch 2 Edition treatment, though specific enhancements have not yet been detailed.

## Fan Frustration and Third-Party Support

The lack of any **Smash Bros. Ultimate** news has predictably ignited discussion within the fan community. Many expected a Switch 2 version or at least a significant update, given the game's immense popularity and sales figures. The announcement of Switch 2 Editions for other games only amplifies this frustration, with some fans questioning Nintendo's priorities. This move towards enhanced editions, rather than full sequels, is a growing trend, as seen with other titles like **Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection**, which is receiving multiple physical editions for various consoles, including a Switch 2 version slated for December 2025. **Angry Video Game Nerd 8-bit** is also securing a Switch release date and physical edition, and **Mouse: P.I. For Hire** will also feature its game on-cartridge for the Switch 2.

## What's Next

While the future of **Super Smash Bros. Ultimate** on Switch 2 remains uncertain, the confirmed enhanced editions and the ongoing trend of third-party support suggest a busy period ahead for the platform. Players can anticipate more details on specific enhancements and release windows for these upgraded titles as the Switch 2's launch approaches.

content_raw: Last October, I wrote an op-ed for this very website presenting my case for a Nintendo Switch 2 Edition of Super Smash Bros. Ultimate. At the time, I thought it was a slam dunk; of the top 10 best-selling games on the original Nintendo Switch, Smash Bros.--which is currently still the third best-selling Switch 1 game ever as of June 30--was the only one to not see any Switch 2-related update, let alone a Nintendo Switch 2 Edition. Today, with the latest Nintendo Direct behind us, that fact remains true, to the point that Nintendo's own website doesn't list Super Smash Bros. Ultimate on its list of " free updates for select Nintendo Switch games ." Nearly five years after Sora's reveal trailer , and his addition to the game, which marked the final update to Ultimate, Smash Bros. has become a dormant franchise. There were some Switch 2 Editions revealed during the Nintendo Direct, so Nintendo hasn't reached the end of the well yet. Here are the games that did add "Nintendo Switch 2 Edition" to their names. New Nintendo Switch 2 Editions Six games are now getting the Switch 2 bump after today's Direct: three first-party titles and three third-party games. The first one revealed with Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment Definitive Edition, which will include all Expansion Pass DLC, improved visuals and frame rate, more enemies on screen during battles, and a new ultra-hard Calamity Mode. While the name says "Definitive Edition," Nintendo describes it as an "enhanced Nintendo Switch 2 version." Next was perhaps the most surprising of the three first-party upgrades: Pikmin 4. Voice commands for the dog Oatchi and a new Dandori Academy mode will be added to the game on November 12. Xenoblade Chronicles 3 was the third first-party game to receive the Switch 2 Edition treatment. The upgraded version will add a new hero called Shimmer, and a Hero's Vault mode where players fight through waves of enemies in order to enhance the party's abilities. On the third-party side, The Witcher 3's upcoming Remastered Edition will hit Switch 2 in September, while cozy sim Palia will add seasonal updates, community events and new Echo Expeditions with its Switch 2 Edition in December. Finally, Crisis Core - Final Fantasy VII Reunion, which originally launched for Nintendo Switch in 2022, joined the Switch 2 Edition family today at the end of the Direct. An Ultimate omission All of those games getting new enhanced editions is cool! The Switch 2 has proven to be a very viable platform for the resurgence of older games. However, there is a glaring hole where the Super Smash Bros. Ultimate Nintendo Switch 2 Edition should be standing, and it's puzzling to say the least. What, if anything, could be holding Nintendo back? Now, the existence of an all-new Smash Bros. was rumored in the lead-up to today's Direct, along with a new Nintendogs and 3D Mario.
